core_obligations: Assume alpha is not a natural number (part 1) resp. not a non-positive integer (part 2). The task is to show that for every admissible direction theta the Laplace-type integral phi_theta(tau) = 2(alpha-1) int_0^{infinity e^{i theta}} (1+zeta)^{alpha-2} e^{-zeta/tau} dzeta is the 1-sum of phi-hat(tau), and similarly for phi_theta(tau) with kernel (1-zeta)^{-alpha}; the proof computes the formal Borel transforms B_1 phi-hat and B_1 phi-hat, observes that they converge near the origin with finite radius, continues them, and verifies Borel-summability in the stated directions, including the holomorphy of the result on the unbounded resp. bounded disc D_theta resp. D_theta(1).
proof_roadmap: Step 1: compute the two formal Borel transforms from the series defined by Proposition for. Step 2: convergence near the origin with finite radius of convergence. Step 3: continue along the direction theta and verify the Laplace representation, giving 1-summability. Step 4: the holomorphy statement on D_theta (Re alpha <= 2) resp. D_theta(1) (otherwise).
